on 21 July, 2023

Santosh Kumar Vishwakarma Pet
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh Respondent(s)

(For Admission and I.R. and Ia No.132061/2023-CONDONATION Of Delay
 In Filing and Ia No.132062/2023-EXEMPTION From Filing O.T. and Ia
 No.132060/2023-EXEMPTION From Surrendering Within Time )
 Date : 21-07-2023 This petition was called on for hearing today.
Coram : Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Manoj Misra

[In Chamber]
 For Petitioner(s) Mr. Dushyant Parashar, Aor
 Mr. Dinesh Pandey, Adv.
 Mr. Manu Parashar, Adv.
 Mr. Muthu M Velpalani, Adv.
 For Respondent(s)

Upon hearing the counsel the Court made the following
 O R D E R

By way of this application, the petitioner seeks exemption from surrendering pursuant to the final judgment and order of the High Court of Madhya Pradesh at Jabalpur, dated 12.05.2022, in Criminal Appeal No. 2387 of 1997, whereby the criminal appeal of the petitioner has been dismissed and 7 years sentence awarded to him by the trial court, under Section 376 of the Indian Penal Code,
1860, has been upheld.

entities.text: High Court of Madhya Pradesh at Jabalpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that petitioner was a 16:15:34 IST Reason: juvenile on the date of the incident and, therefore, he is entitled to the benefit of juvenility and, accordingly, this is a fit case to grant him exemption from surrendering pursuant to the order of the High Court.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: I have perused the judgment rendered in Criminal Appeal No. 2387 of 1997.
It does not indicate that the plea of juvenility was specifically raised by the appellant-therein.
Though, there is no bar to raise such plea before this Court.
But, if raised, it would be considered at an appropriate stage.

Consequently, since the applicant has been convicted for an offence punishable under Section 376 IPC, I do not find it to be a fit case to grant exemption to the applicant from surrendering pursuant to the order of conviction as aforementioned.
I.A. No. 132060 of 2023 is, accordingly, dismissed.
However, the petitioner is granted three weeks time to surrender pursuant to the order of the High Court.
Any observation in this order shall not prejudice the claim/ plea taken by the applicant for juvenility, as and when the same is considered at the appropriate stage.

(POOJA SHARMA) (R.S. NARAYANAN)
